Sabey Data Centers' SDC Ashburn campus sits in Loudoun County's "Data Center Alley," with this building, Building A, at 21735 Red Rum Drive, Ashburn, Virginia, per OpenStreetMap address data corroborated against the operator's own Ashburn location page. Sabey is one of seven data center campuses the company operates nationally as of 2026. Sabey traces its roots to 1972, when Dave Sabey founded Sabey Corporation as a Pacific Northwest commercial real estate developer; the company entered the data center business almost by accident during the dot-com collapse, when a vacated tenant building in Seattle became SDC Seattle Building 5. Sabey Data Centers itself was formally established in 2010 as a joint venture between Sabey Corporation and institutional investor National Real Estate Advisors, a structure confirmed on both the operator's own site and independently by Wikipedia.

Building A sits alongside neighboring Buildings B (21745 Red Rum Drive) and C (21741 Red Rum Drive) on the same Red Rum Drive block. Per Wikipedia's most recent coverage of the company, the Ashburn campus has grown to include a third building under construction, with roughly 85 MW of total planned campus capacity once complete, though that figure is not broken out per building and is not assigned to this structure specifically. Sabey markets its data center facilities, including Ashburn, as carrying SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and SSAE 18 compliance attestations, per the operator's own site; those attestations describe compliance posture rather than physical capacity.

Sabey's national footprint as of this writing spans Seattle and the Columbia River region (Quincy and East Wenatchee, Washington, powered by hydroelectricity), Ashburn, Manhattan (Intergate Manhattan at 375 Pearl Street, opened 2013 in a retrofitted former Verizon/NY Telephone switching building), the Austin, Texas metro area (a first Round Rock building completed October 2024), and a planned Umatilla, Oregon campus exceeding 100 MW. Tim Mirick became Sabey's president effective January 1, 2025, succeeding Rob Rockwood, per Wikipedia.
